points.text: Gain largely due to learned per-node embedding; baselines' node identity input undefined.
Spatial reconstruction near-trivial under random token masking; dual objective not exercised.
Unseen-placement generalization tested on one scene with reused embeddings; baselines lack protocol.
Margins within std on HAR and Ridgecrest, yet called best overall.
Near-zero baseline scores in Table 2 suggest failed head training.
Prop. 3.1 lower bounds on different quantities cannot rank methods; assumptions unspecified.
No test split, undisclosed selection, pretraining may include evaluation clips.
Catalog description lists physically impossible label ranges.
Overstated wording: 'significantly advances', 'solid theoretical foundations', 'synergistic effect'.
Table 2 caption thresholds mismatch columns.
HAR body positions inconsistent between Section 4.3 and appendix.
Node-balanced masking 'slight improvement' is within noise.
Model size, optimizer, learning rate, epochs, compute and code missing.
How baselines read multi-node input is not described.
Abstract/intro overclaim relative to results (advances, theory, synergy, arbitrary placement).
Key ablation and unseen-placement results relegated to appendix.
Theory section long, assumptions unstated, no testable prediction.
Closest prior art using sensor identity/geometry in MAE cited but not compared.
Novelty distinction contradicted by paper's own citations (LEGO, NeRF).
Method combines known components; structural position is a low-rank node-ID embedding.
Propositions restate standard variational bound and Kong et al. result.
Theory gives lower bounds not shown tighter; prose conclusions do not follow; assumptions hidden.
Prop. 3.2 spatial contrastive pair is vacuous since positions are broadcast.
No published reference numbers to calibrate authors' baseline runs.
Adaptation of CAV-MAE to non-audio-visual sensor data undescribed.
Characterization of reference [70] questionable.
Headline gain attributable to per-node embedding baselines may lack; need matched baselines.
Claim of resilience to scarce labels contradicted by larger relative degradation.
Message-drop gap within std; lower errors than Table 1 unexplained; drop application unstated.
SPAR degrades more on unseen placements; margin over baselines shrinks.
Gains within seed noise on two datasets; no statistical tests.
No test split, undisclosed selection, possibly transductive pretraining on evaluation scenes.
No hyperparameters, compute, parameter counts or code; not compute-matched.
No supervised-from-scratch, trivial predictor or domain locator baselines.
Minor: caption mismatch, body positions, PhyMask family, MSE undefined.
Impossible magnitude and depth ranges in catalog.
Centralized joint encoder conflicts with distributed sensing; no communication/compute cost.
Assumes accurate known coordinates; no coordinate-noise test.
Per-sample normalization removes absolute scale; unclear handling of spatial scales.
Time synchronization across nodes assumed but not stated.
Signal propagation physics left entirely to learning.
No classical physics-based locators or supervised baseline.
Dual-use and privacy issues not discussed.
Define mAP@r thresholds in Table 2 caption.
Novelty limited: standard embeddings, LLM as preprocessing, dual reconstruction well established.
Manual normalization of spatial inputs unjustified given learned embedding.
Structural position concept not clearly defined; semantic capture unclear.
No specification or analysis of datasets where structural attributes matter.
Prop. 3.1 hard to follow; weak connection to claims and method.
Unclear whether baseline results reimplemented or taken from papers.
Extremely poor baseline performance in Table 2 unexplained.
LLM component evaluated only on HAR with minimal gain.
No runtime or computational complexity reported.
What 'structural' factors are remains unclear; paper opaque to outsiders.
Contrastive interpretation with identical S and R in positive pairs makes little sense.
Unclear what spatial/structural information each method accesses at evaluation; possible unfair advantage.
Generalization and ablation experiments supporting main claims only in appendix.
Claimed generalization across downstream tasks not shown.
Experimental validation listed as separate contribution.
'Duality' between positions and signals is questionable terminology.
Minor: Eq. 6 citation, summing vs concatenation phrasing, figure order.
Theory forced, restates setup, does not explain empirical findings.
Restricting baselines to small pretraining data may undercut their scalability advantage.
Unseen sensor placement deserves more detailed study.
Insights from Figure 3 visualizations unclear.
Redundant phrasing at line 348.
Comparisons unfair since baselines do not use spatial information.
Model size/complexity not reported in comparisons or ablations.

P.summary: Gain may stem from node-identity/spatial input baselines lack; baseline input pipeline undescribed.
Spatial reconstruction trivial under random masking.
Unseen-placement evaluation limited and margin shrinks.
Margins within noise; no significance tests.
Baselines in Table 2 appear to have failed training.
Theory does not establish claimed advantages; assumptions unstated.
No test split, undisclosed selection, possible transductive pretraining.
Impossible label ranges in earthquake catalog.
Abstract and intro overclaim.
Minor caption and consistency errors.
Hyperparameters, compute and code missing.
Key results relegated to appendix.
Closest sensor-ID/geometry MAE prior art not compared.
Novelty modest; distinctions contradicted; structural position is node-ID embedding.
Propositions restate known results.
Prop. 3.2 contrastive reading vacuous for spatial branch.
No published reference numbers for baselines.
CAV-MAE adaptation undescribed.
Questionable citation characterization.
Label-scarcity robustness overclaimed.
Message-drop results unclear and within noise.
Missing supervised, trivial and classical baselines.
Centralized design conflicts with distributed sensing; no cost analysis.
Accurate coordinates assumed; no noise test.
Normalization removes absolute scale.
Time synchronization assumption unstated.
Propagation physics not modelled.
Dual-use and privacy undiscussed.

Q.summary: No analysis of when structural attributes matter.
Theory weakly connected to method and results.
Runtime, complexity and model size unreported.
Contrastive pairs share identical S and R.
Unfair information access: baselines lack spatial/structural inputs.
Baselines restricted to small pretraining data.
